info.bio: The Doobie Brothers es una banda estadounidense de rock and roll, formada en 1970 por Johnston, John Hartman y el bajista Greg Murph, que luego fue sustituido por Dave Shogren; todos ellos de California. En el año siguiente, ya transformados en quinteto (con Trian Porter y el percusionista Mike Hossack), lanzaron su primer LP Doobie Brothers. El sonido que hacían era un estilo country rock, con algo de tendencia hacia el gospel y con la utilización de instrumentos de viento.

scenes.name: Country-rock y roots-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: En los setenta, el reajuste a los viejos valores (blues, folk, country) convierte al rock en uno de los mayores éxitos del consumismo: el Establishment ya no intenta destruirlo, lo absorbe. El country-rock de Gram Parsons es una moda enorme: Commander Cody, New Riders Of The Purple Sage, Manassas, Nitty Gritty Dirt Band, Poco y los Eagles (Desperado, Hotel California); en Nashville surgen los «outlaws» (Waylon Jennings, Willie Nelson, Kris Kristofferson). El roots-rock sigue con Hot Tuna, Little Feat y Doobie Brothers, y la nostalgia recupera el blues (Roy Buchanan, Bonnie Raitt), la armonía vocal (Manhattan Transfer, Roches, McGarrigle Sisters) y los cincuenta (American Graffiti).

podcast.title: Live Performance Concerns (1973)
podcast.body: The Doobie Brothers, like other rock bands of the era, expressed concern about performing live on *The Midnight Special* without lip-syncing, worried about how their sound would translate. However, their performance "didn't sound so bad" and was part of the show's appeal in offering authentic live music. "Now one of the things that rock bands worried about with the Midnight special and the fact that they were not going to be lip syncing is what they would sound like live."

podcast.title: Considered for Soviet Tour
podcast.body: The Doobie Brothers were considered as potential candidates for the first American band to tour the Soviet Union in 1977 but were ultimately passed over in favor of the Nitty Gritty Dirt Band. This initiative was part of a US effort to use rock and roll to undermine communism through cultural exchange. "In 1977, the nitty-gritty dirt band was chosen over the Dubie brothers, and the soft rock band America, must have been their name, to be the first American band to tour through the Soviet Union."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unintentional Religious Following
podcast.body: The Doobie Brothers' cover of "Jesus Is Just Alright" was not recorded with religious intent; band member Tom Johnston stated they were "just musicians outplaying a gig." However, the song's popularity attracted religious fans, known as "one-wayers," who would attend their shows, point their fingers skyward, and even throw scriptures onto the stage, much to the band's initial confusion. "Little did they know they were trying to enlist the support of the wrong guys."

concerts.title: The Midnight Special (1973)
concerts.body: The Doobie Brothers made their television debut on episode four of *The Midnight Special*. They performed "Jesus Is Just Alright" and "Listen to the Music" live, overcoming concerns about how they would sound without lip-syncing. "One of those bands that made their television debut on the Midnight special was the Dubie Brothers who appeared on episode four, four out of four 50."

xref.title: First American Band to Tour Soviet Union (1977)
xref.body: In 1977, the Nitty Gritty Dirt Band was chosen over more conventional acts like the Doobie Brothers and America to be the first American band to tour the Soviet Union. This tour, endorsed by President Jimmy Carter, aimed to undermine communism through rock and roll. The tour proved immensely successful among young people in Russia and other Soviet republics, generating such high demand for tickets that it overwhelmed the KGB. "To be the first American band to tour through the Soviet Union, President Jimmy Carter was all for this, thinking that rock and roll could undermine communism."

xref.title: Lighting Roadie Turned Band Member
xref.body: In 1976, while working as a lighting roadie for The Doobie Brothers, Bobby LaKind was observed playing congas on stage. The band was impressed by his skills and invited him to assist in the studio. His contributions were so successful that he became a full member of the band in 1979. "Back in 1976, the Dubie Brothers noticed lighting roadie Bobby Lackind messing around with some congas on stage. You're pretty good, they said. You want to help out in the studio? He did and that worked out so well that in 1979 he was made a full member of the band."

xref.title: Post-Breakup Member Destinies
xref.body: After Clover broke up in 1978, its members pursued various paths. One individual joined The Doobie Brothers before eventually quitting music to become a chiropractor. Another member achieved recognition by writing the song "867-5309/Jenny" for Tommy Tutone. Additionally, two members, along with Clover's singer (who had merely hung around during the Elvis Costello sessions), went on to form the successful band Huey Lewis and the News. "Clover broke up in 1978. One guy joined the Dubie Brothers before quitting music to become a chiropractor, and another guy wrote the song 867-5309-Geni for Tommy Tutone."

xref.title: Versatile Session Musician
xref.body: Beyond Motown, Bobby Jean Hall has an impressive client list that includes a diverse range of legendary artists. Her percussion work has graced albums by Bob Dylan, Lynyrd Skynyrd, Rod Stewart, Janis Joplin, Joni Mitchell, Dolly Parton, The Doobie Brothers, Aretha Franklin, Tracy Chapman, James Taylor, and Stevie Nicks, highlighting her status as a highly sought-after session player. "Other clients have included Bob Dylan, Leonard Skinner, Rod Stewart, Janice Joplin, Joni Mitchell, Dolly Parton, The Dooby Brothers, Aretha Franklin, Tracy Chapman, James Taylor, and Stevie Nicks."
